name: Tidemark
summary: A macOS menu-bar app that tracks how long you've spent in each app and nudges you when a focus block runs long.
metaTitle: App-usage timer & focus nudges for Mac

sections.title: Live timeline
sections.description: Tidemark sits in the menu bar and records the frontmost app every few seconds. The timeline shows your day as a stacked bar — one glance tells you where the hours went, no manual timers to start or stop.

images.caption: A full day, app by app

sections.title: Focus nudges
sections.description: Set a soft limit per app. When you cross it, Tidemark taps you on the shoulder instead of locking you out — the choice to keep going stays yours.

images.caption: A nudge after 90 minutes in the browser

sections.title: Local-first
sections.description: Everything stays on your Mac. No account, no sync server, no telemetry — the data never leaves the device, and you can export it as CSV whenever you want.

faqs.question: What is Tidemark?
faqs.answer: A macOS menu-bar app that tracks how long you spend in each app and nudges you when a focus block runs long. It records the frontmost app automatically — no timers to start — and shows your day as a stacked timeline.

faqs.question: How is it different from Screen Time?
faqs.answer: Screen Time reports after the fact, across devices. Tidemark is live and Mac-local: it nudges you the moment you cross a per-app limit, and keeps every second on your machine with a CSV export whenever you want it.

faqs.question: Is my data private?
faqs.answer: Yes. Everything stays on your Mac — no account, no sync server, no telemetry. The data never leaves the device, and you can export it as CSV anytime.

faqs.question: How much does Tidemark cost?
faqs.answer: A monthly subscription or a one-time lifetime purchase on the Mac App Store. Both unlock every feature; the lifetime option is for people who'd rather pay once.
